column1: # The managed assemblies the game ships besides its own code (Moonlighter_Data/Managed), run through tools/translate
# as the game's Assembly-CSharp is (`mltranslate survey-assembly`, tools/translate/AssemblySurvey.cs): decompiled with the
# same lowered settings, compiled by Roslyn against the DLLs they reference, every type translated in memory with
# tools/translate/bindings.tsv (less its bindings of the surveyed assembly's own types). Each row is an API of ANOTHER
# assembly one of them uses that bindings.tsv doesn't bind. Sorted by assembly, then lines blocked.
#   api_assembly  the assembly defining the API (UnityEngine.CoreModule, mscorlib, UnityEngine.UI for TextMeshPro...)
#   native        native: the engine implements it (an InternalCall method, an accessor that is one, or a wrapper
#                   of one in an engine module: a body calling an X_Injected/INTERNAL_ icall, or a body of at most 48
#                   IL bytes calling a native one and otherwise only code reaching no icall, as an overload forwarding
#                   to one through a conversion); a type: a class of an engine
#                   module deriving from UnityEngine.Object, or a class with icalls (a native pointer inside).
#                 managed: C# in that assembly (translatable like the game's code; for a method, `detail` lists
#                   the icalls its body reaches through its managed calls, 8 levels deep; structs and enums are
#   kind          as in unity_api_gaps.tsv: type (no C++ mapping), get/set (a property), call, new (a constructor),
#                   op (an operator or conversion), field, event/add/remove, delegate (a method as a delegate), base
#   methods/lines the surveyed assembly's methods (their decompiled C# lines) using it; a method missing several APIs
#                   counts for each; 0: only named in declarations (a field's or a signature's type)
#   classes       the surveyed assembly's files (top-level types) with such methods
#   detail        how it is native (icall, the icalls a wrapper reaches, [its UnityEngine.Bindings attributes]),
#                   the icalls a managed body reaches, or what kind of type it is
# Totals ("translate today": every construct supported and every API bound):

#   UnityEngine.UI: 112 top-level types (192 with nested and compiler-generated), 112 files, 19476 decompiled lines; 1728 methods (14368 lines): 1264 translate today (73.1%; lines 45.7%), 459 need bindings (327 need a native API, 119 only managed and BCL ones, 13 only BCL ones), 5 unsupported; 426 APIs missing (191 native, 210 managed, 25 BCL); Roslyn errors 0

#   TextMeshPro-2017.3-Runtime: 93 top-level types (135 with nested and compiler-generated), 90 files, 24826 decompiled lines; 1308 methods (20033 lines): 775 translate today (59.3%; lines 25.7%), 532 need bindings (202 need a native API, 293 only managed and BCL ones, 37 only BCL ones), 1 unsupported; 376 APIs missing (122 native, 218 managed, 36 BCL); Roslyn errors 12

#   DOTween: 95 top-level types (186 with nested and compiler-generated), 94 files, 14381 decompiled lines; 1107 methods (11237 lines): 936 translate today (84.6%; lines 79.3%), 169 need bindings (106 need a native API, 43 only managed and BCL ones, 20 only BCL ones), 2 unsupported; 131 APIs missing (71 native, 25 managed, 35 BCL); Roslyn errors 215
